{{NAME_1}}.role: a child who acts like a reporter with Kabir and asks 35 friends how many hours a day they watch TV (the book gives no pronoun)

{{NAME_2}}.role: the other child reporter; records the answers of 35 friends in a notebook (the book gives no pronoun)

{{NAME_3}}.role: the shopkeeper the children call Joseph Uncle; takes stock of toys, board games and sports items and tries a pictograph (the book says 'his store')

{{NAME_4}}.role: Joseph Uncle's helper; suggests one icon for every 5 items (the book says 'one of his helpers')

{{NAME_5}}.role: notes the number of two-wheelers passing her house in one hour on three days (the book says 'her house')

{{NAME_6}}.role: records his daily routine in a table of squares (one square = 1 hour); the book gives no pronoun

{{NAME_7}}.role: records her daily routine as a bar graph (the book says 'I have shown...' and 'her routine')

{{NAME_8}}.role: stays in a residential school and sees the food wastage notice (the book says 'Her school')

_note_kin: Uncle in 'Joseph Uncle' is a kin word, not a name: write Joseph Uncle as {{NAME_3}} Uncle. The unnamed children of the pictures (the girl with the thought bubble, the children of the notebook and of the True or False picture) have no token.
